name: Multisensory Design
short_description: How sensory channels combine, compete, and compensate in architectural experience, determining the coherence or conflict of environmental perception.

components.name: Congruency Enhancement
components.description: When visual, auditory, haptic, and olfactory cues are congruent, the environmental experience is enhanced beyond any single channel.

components.name: Inverse Effectiveness
components.description: When one sensory channel is degraded, multisensory integration compensates more strongly.

components.name: Haptic-Material Perception
components.description: Surface material properties drive haptic exploration and affective evaluation of architectural surfaces.

components.name: Thalamic Filtering
components.description: The pulvinar nucleus selectively gates multisensory information flow, filtering environmental salience.

components.name: Crossmodal Binding
components.description: Crossmodal correspondences (e.g., bright spaces 'feeling' lighter) shape environmental perception.

design_implications: Ensure sensory cues are congruent: warm lighting with warm materials, not cold fluorescent with wood.
In acoustically degraded spaces, enhance visual and haptic channels to compensate.
Design material palettes that reward haptic exploration (varied textures at hand height).
Avoid sensory conflict zones where visual openness contradicts acoustic enclosure.

confidence_intervals.note: Effect sizes for congruent vs incongruent multisensory environments on comfort and performance.
